Definition: from a derivative of ἰς (force; compare ἔσχον, a form of G2192); forcefulness (literally or figuratively):--ability, might(-ily), power, strength.
BiblicalUsage: Strength is what God gives and what he is owed, and the Bible holds both together. In Ephesians 6:10 Paul says, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might, in Mark 12:30 Jesus says to love the Lord with all thy strength, in 1 Peter 4:11 the speaker speaks as the oracles of God, that God in all things may be glorified, and in Revelation 5:12 the Lamb is worthy to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that strength flows one way first: God gives it, and I spend it loving him. Heaven gives it back to the Lamb who was slain.
RelatedEvents: The Greatest Commandment; The Throne Room and the Lamb
